 Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the NWKRTC (hereinafter referred to as 'the Corporation', for short) challenging the judgment and award dated 23.08.2012 passed by the learned District Judge and MACT, Gadag, in MVC No.333/2010.

2. Facts giving rise to filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 09.12.2009 at about 07:30 pm on Gadag- Mundaragi road near Adavisomapur village, the claimant was proceeding towards Gadag on his bicycle and when he came in front of Shivam Petrol Bunk, at that time, one KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA.19/F.2046, driven by its driver, came in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and while overtaking another vehicle hit to the bicycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.

As a result, the petitioner sustained severe injuries and NC: 2024:KHC-D:18000 immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Gadag and then to Dr. Shirol Nursing Home,
Gadag and he has permanently become disabled.
Hence, the claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
3. Upon service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel.
Respondent No.2 filed objections denying the averments made in the claim petition.
4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the petition awarding compensation of Rs.1,68,120/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Being aggrieved, present appeal has been filed by insurance company.

The learned counsel appearing for the corporation contended that, that as per the claim petition,
at the time of the accident, he was aged 32 years but the Tribunal has considered the age of the The Divisional Manager vs Yallappa Ningappa Kari on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104660439/
2 claimant as 23 and awarded compensation which is on the higher side.

sentences.text: He further contended that considering the evidence of the Doctor, the injuries suffered by the claimant and the medical records, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities and other incidental expenses are on the higher side.
6. Respondent No.1 is served and unrepresented.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant/corporation and perused the judgment and award.
8.

It is not in dispute that the claimant has suffered injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.12.2009 due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC bearing registration No.KA.19/F.2046.
As NC: 2024:KHC-D:18000 per the petition averments, the claimant is aged 32 years at the time of the accident, however, the disability certificate mentions the age of the claimant as 23 years.
In the claim petition, due to typographical error the age of the claimant might be shown as 32 years.

Considering the evidence of the parties, the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the age of the claimant was 23 years at the time of the accident and on considering his avocation and disability, has granted just and reasonable compensation.

Hence, the following order:
The appeal is dismissed.
The judgment and award dated 23.08.2012 passed by the learned District Judge and MACT, Gadag, in MVC No.333/2010 is upheld.
Registry is directed to transfer the amount in deposit to the Tribunal concerned.

Sd/-
